For any competing ellipsoid including nonzero center, squared support constraints give \(\operatorname{tr}(AS)+c^{\mathsf T}Ac\le m\); determinant AM-GM proves global maximal volume and uniqueness. Root-of-unity factorization yields the exact volume. Strict logdet concavity and spectral moments prove the universal \(t=1/\sqrt2\) threshold, \(C^1\)-but-not-\(C^2\) sharp second derivatives \(-2m\) and \(-10m\); the scalar-root limit proves the large-m rate. Executed 276 spectral/contact/determinant tests, 47 moment identities and 20 full-matrix numerical optimizations. Tests are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The maximum inscribed volume and ellipsoid contact structure are natural Banach-space geometric invariants. The theorem resolves an infinite continuous wheel-metric family, identifies the dimension-independent boundary separating spherical and Laplacian contact regimes, and proves a non-removable second-derivative jump \(-8m\). The limiting volume rate preserves that phase transition. This is a structural parameter law, not an arbitrary finite calculation or a restatement of the known unit-weight special case.
